newsitem.title: USA: US budget plan has $140 bln gross tax cut -- Hobson.
newsitem.headline: US budget plan has $140 bln gross tax cut -- Hobson.

text.p: U.S. Rep. David Hobson, a Republican from Ohio, said a proposed budget framework presented to House Republicans Thursday included $85 billion to $90 billion in net tax cuts and $140 billion to $145 billion in gross tax cuts over five years.
The plan included $60 billion in increased spending and $115 billion in Medicare savings over five years, Hobson told reporters.
The proposal also included $200 billion in entitlement savings over the first five years, which would balloon to $700 billion to $800 billion in savings over 10 years, Hobson said.
The plan had Medicaid savings of about $25 billion to $35 billion, he said.

The tax portion of a budget pact was expected to include a capital gains tax cut, estate tax reduction and a $500 child tax credit, Hobson said. Also likely to be included would be provisions for child health and tuition, he said.
Rep W.J. Tauzin, a Louisiana Republican, said that if there were anything related to the consumer price index in the plan, it would not be a "legislative fix."
